name: steam_reheat_power_plant_arrays
title: Steam reheat power plant with T-s arrays (Cengel exercise 10-34b)
summary: Steady reheat Rankine cycle on water, the array form of the 80 MW exercise. Saturated liquid is pumped from 10 kPa to 10 MPa, heated to 500 °C, expanded to 1 MPa, reheated once to 500 °C and expanded to 10 kPa. Saturation states and the T[i], s[i] arrays trace the cycle. The model returns the thermal efficiency and the steam mass flow.

origin.course: KU Leuven thermodynamics; textbook exercise Cengel 10-34b

verification.summary: compare_solution.py against the stored solution of 10-34b.EES, no --ees-units: 74 common variables, 1 differ (rtol=0.001); only in EES: 0; only in CoolSolve: 0. The one difference is x_8 (EES 100, CoolSolve 0), the EES superheated quality sentinel; it feeds no equation. All other variables are within 5.60e-04. Net power 80 MW, efficiency 0.3405, steam flow 62.65 kg/s.
verification.reference: EES stored solution of 10-34b.EES (compare_solution.py, units already SI)
verification.notes: Summary line: 74 common variables, 1 differ (rtol=0.001); only in EES: 0; only in CoolSolve: 0. The printed maximum over all 74 common variables is 1.00e+00 on x_8. EES quality() stores 100 on superheated vapour (CS-GAP-QUALITY-DOME); CoolSolve returns 0. x_8 is an output of quality() and feeds no other equation. The next largest relative difference is h_3 at 5.60e-04. Water enthalpy residuals are property differences, not a constant shift: about −28 J/kg on the compressed liquid (h_1, h_2) and +101 to +1129 J/kg on vapour and saturation enthalpies (largest absolute residual h_5, +1129 J/kg). The ees_variables.csv units column is blank and the stored enthalpies are already in J, so --ees-units was not used. Equation residuals of the energy balances are below 1e-5 W and 4e-7 J/kg. The linked binary mtime is 2026-10-15 20:47, commit 5a522f7; an uncommitted parser.cpp change about REPEAT in the main program was linked with it. This file has no REPEAT.
